newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy phone price cut barely hits CPI - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Italy phone price cut barely hits CPI - ministry.

text.p: Reductions in telephone charges, to be introduced by the end of September, will help cut inflation by just 0.01 percentage points, under-secretary at the Post ministry, Michele Lauria, said in a statement on Friday.
"The negative impact on the consumer price index will be 0.01 percent on a year-on-year basis," the statement said.
The forecast was based on a calculation made by national statistics office Istat, it said.

Telephone charges account for 1.1889 percent of Istat's inflation basket. Preliminary CPI data released last week indicated a 3.3-3.4 percent year-on-year rise in August inflation, compared with a 3.6-percent rise in July.
The tariff revision for fixed-line telephones was announced in July. A slight overhaul in some mobile phone tariffs was announced on Thursday.
